accessDenied.cause2b: That is the case for an account promoted to administrator after migration

users.title: Account & user directory
users.description: Central management of Ifriqiya Soccer Star profiles: consultation, assignment, status moderation and activity traceability. Opening a record gives access to editing, suspension, reactivation and deletion.
users.searchPlaceholder: Filter by name, email or phone…
users.suspendDesc: The business profile moves to “suspended”: on its next start, the app signs the user out. A session already open keeps working — this is reversible from their record.
users.noteSuspendBody: Suspending deactivates the account and moves its profile to “suspended”. Nothing touches authentication: a session already open keeps working until the app restarts, which then reads the profile status and signs the user out.
users.noteReactivateBody: A reactivated account goes back to “awaiting approval”, itself a blocking status: the file returns to the queue instead of regaining access along the way. The rule is enforced by the database, not by this screen.
users.noteDeletionBody: A request made from the app is only recorded: it erases nothing. Permanent deletion remains a manual action from the account record — it removes access and data, and it is irreversible.

validations.title: Profile approval queues
validations.description: Pending accounts, in arrival order. Approving a player or professional profile unlocks access to the app: it is the profile status that opens it, not the identity document's.
validations.metricDelayHint: Between a document's upload and its review
validations.metricRefusedHint: Player profiles sent back with a reason
validations.metricApprovalHint: Over {count} decision(s) in the last 30 days
validations.searchPlaceholder: Filter by name, club or nationality…
validations.noteUnlockBody: The mobile app decides whether to let a user in based on their profile status — player or professional — and on nothing else. Until that profile is approved, it sends them back to the waiting screen, whatever the state of their documents.
validations.noteIdentityBody: Reviewing an identity document is a check separate from approving the account. Accepting the document does not grant access: the two actions are deliberately separate, and rejecting a document requires a reason, which is passed on to the person.
validations.noteReversibleBody: A rejected file goes back to its author with the reason written here. It returns to this queue as soon as it is fixed: nothing is erased, and the status history stays readable on the account record.
validations.playersEmptyDesc: New files will appear here as soon as a player completes their KYC step.
validations.rejectPlayerDesc: The reason is recorded on the profile and serves as the explanation given to the player.
validations.playerRailFootnote: As soon as the profile moves to “approved”, the app lets the player in, and their profile becomes visible to recruiters if visibility is on. Accepting the identity document is not enough: these are two separate actions.
validations.noIdentityUploaded: No identity document uploaded for this account.
validations.prosPanelDesc: Check the documents before approving: an approved account gets access to the player database. Opening a row loads its file on the right.
validations.prosEmptyDesc: Files arrive here once the professional documents have been uploaded.
validations.rejectProDesc: The reason is recorded on the account and passed on to the professional.
validations.requestChangesDesc: The account goes back to the incomplete status and the professional receives what to fix.
validations.proRailFootnote: An approved professional account gets access to the player database and can open a Scout Day. Approving the organisation and approving its documents are two separate actions: the account status is the one the app reads.
validations.docsPanelDesc: One status per document. An account can stay pending as long as one document is undecided.
validations.docsEmptyDesc: Every uploaded document has been examined.
validations.docDossierDesc: The document, the account that uploaded it, and the other documents in the same file.
validations.identityPanelDesc: Note: this queue is about reviewing identity documents, which is separate from the player profile status. Approving here does not approve the account — the profile also has to be approved in the “Player profiles” queue.
validations.identityEmptyDesc: KYC files uploaded from the app will arrive here.
validations.identityDossierDesc: The document and the declared information it has to match.
validations.rejectIdentityDesc: The reason is recorded on the document and passed on to the player.
